steps.title: Load the MovR demo database
steps.narration: cockroach workload init movr creates the ride-sharing schema and data on the 3-node cluster.

steps.title: Run the MovR workload
steps.narration: Leave this running. The chart plots ops/sec from the workload. Wait for a steady line before dropping the index.

steps.title: Drop the vehicle index on rides
steps.narration: The foreign key uses this index, so the constraint comes off first. Vehicle lookups then scan rides, and throughput should fall. Leave the workload running.
sql: ALTER TABLE movr.rides DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS fk_vehicle_city_ref_vehicles;

steps.title: Ask the MCP server which index is missing
steps.prompt: The MovR workload on the rides table got slower after an index was dropped. Which index is missing, and what should I create to restore it?
steps.narration: Wait until the chart has fallen, then send the suggested question. The Cursor agent calls the CockroachDB MCP server and should name the missing rides index.
sql: The MovR workload on the rides table got slower after an index was dropped. Which index is missing, and what should I create to restore it?

steps.title: Put the rides vehicle index back
steps.narration: Creating the same key columns lets the workload use the index again. Throughput should climb back while MovR is still running.
sql: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS rides_auto_index_fk_vehicle_city_ref_vehicles ON movr.rides (vehicle_city, vehicle_id);
